brief.why: A support bot is only as good as the tools it can call. Order status is the most common question customers ask.
brief.done_looks_like: get_order_status(order_id) returns the status for a known order, raises a clear error for an unknown one, and a TOOLS spec describes the tool so a model knows when to use it.
brief.you_start_with: An empty support_agent.py and a small stub dictionary of orders. No network and no API key.

brief.why: Refunds move money, so the tool must check its inputs and the bot must pick the right tool from its description, not from keywords.
brief.done_looks_like: issue_refund(order_id, amount) refunds within policy, refuses amounts over the order total and orders already refunded, and TOOLS describes both tools with no keyword routing.
brief.you_start_with: Your order-status tool from milestone 1 and the same stub orders.

red_flag_rules.description: Picks a tool by checking for a keyword in the question instead of describing the tool to the model.
Returns a fixed status string for a specific order id instead of looking it up.

criteria: Each tool has a description that says when to use it and when not to.
The tool is chosen from its description, not from keywords in the question.
Inputs are validated and failures give a clear, specific error.
The learner can explain why the tool is shaped the way it is.

explain: Walk me through what happens when the bot gets 'where is my order 1001?'.
Why does the tool description matter to the model?
change: How would you add a 'cancelled' status without touching the lookup logic?
How would you cap refunds at a different policy limit?
fix: A customer asks 'I want my money back' and the bot calls the order-status tool. What do you check first?
An unknown order id crashes the bot. Where do you fix it?
